      <title>Russian warship sinks in Benghazi after suspected Ukrainian drone attack</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/22/blast-russian-ship-suspected-drone-attack-benghazi-libya</link>
      <description><p>No one has claimed responsibility for the strike on the vessel, which had docked on its way back to Russia</p><p>A Russian warship docked in the Libyan port city of Benghazi was struck in the early hours of Sunday in a suspected Ukrainian sea drone attack, causing a dramatic night-time explosion and the sinking of the vessel.</p><p>The strike severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette that had stopped to refuel and take on supplies, according to Libyan officials from the country’s eastern government.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/22/blast-russian-ship-suspected-drone-attack-benghazi-libya">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/20/california-coastal-communities-alert-big-waves-hit-state</link>
      <description><p>Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded</p><p>Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.</p><p>Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/20/california-coastal-communities-alert-big-waves-hit-state">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/19/baobab-five-trees-south-africa-dug-up-export-blocked-georgia-aoe</link>
      <description><p>The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits</p><p>Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia.</p><p>The baobabs arrived at a reserve in Timbavati, in north-eastern South Africa, on Wednesday, where they will be replanted and supported by cables to help them recover. The trees had been stranded at a warehouse in Durban since July, when they were intercepted by authorities who said they had been moved without the necessary permissions.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/19/baobab-five-trees-south-africa-dug-up-export-blocked-georgia-aoe">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/nov/19/women-girls-rights-rape-sexual-violence-africa-marriage-unfpa</link>
      <description><p>Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds</p><p>One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report.</p><p>In west and central Africa, almost half of women (45%) are not able to say no in their own marriage, while a third of women (33%) in east and southern Africa and in Arab states face the same predicament.       <description><p>New research finds that the British-led Cobre Mining Company helped industrialise Manchester via copper deposits and enslaved African people</p><p>• <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/ng-interactive/2026/sep/16/slave-trade-wealth-britain-financial-system-bank-of-england-enslaved-africans">Slave-trade wealth was embedded in Britain’s financial system, research finds</a></p><p>British businesses run by long-serving directors of the Bank of England profited from “brutal” enslavement in Cuba for decades after slavery’s abolition in the British empire, according to research.</p><p>Men and boys were enslaved in prison conditions at the El Cobre copper ore mine near Santiago de Cuba, which supplied British firms during the Industrial Revolution, the historian Chris Evans has found.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/news/2026/nov/22/bank-of-england-directors-illegally-profited-enslavement-cuba">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/20/race-to-be-next-un-secretary-general-exposes-divisions-among-world-powers</link>
      <description><p>Debate about dominance of permanent five members could reignite if major powers block Costa Rican frontrunner</p><p>The race to become the next UN secretary general could reach a decisive moment on Friday when a UN security council vote is likely to reveal whether the Costa Rican frontrunner for the post would be blocked by the big powers. Each member goes down the list of candidates, casting an “encourage”, “discourage” or “no opinion” vote for each candidate.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/20/race-to-be-next-un-secretary-general-exposes-divisions-among-world-powers">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Anne Twomey says lack of proper debate around bill is ‘flabbergasting’ amid concerns over extension of ministerial powers</p><ul><li><p>Get our <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/email-newsletters?CMP=cvau_sfl">daily political email</a>, <a href="https://app.adjust.com/w4u7jx3">free app</a> or <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/series/full-story?CMP=cvau_sfl">daily news podcast</a></p></li></ul><p>Labor’s new defence bill is “lazy and irresponsible” lawmaking, one of Australia’s leading constitutional scholars has warned, claiming provisions for the government to secretly class any facility as a special security zone could raise serious legal issues.</p><p>The prime minister, Anthony Albanese, claimed on Monday that critics of the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/nov/23/proposed-defence-laws-have-been-described-as-draconian-and-a-war-against-democracy-why-are-people-worried">“accelerating capability and protecting bases” bill</a> were “jump[ing] at shadows”, accusing them of “absurd” claims.       <link>https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/23/gas-prices-in-europe-surge-as-forecast-cold-snap-feeds-supply-shortage-fears</link>
      <description><p>Jump in price follows slowdown in Qatar supplies and depleted summer stocks due to heatwaves</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/live/2026/nov/23/tech-sell-off-ai-stock-market-support-measures-deployed-south-korea-taiwan-china-ftse-nasdaq-latest-news-updates">Business live – latest updates</a></p></li></ul><p>European gas prices surged on Monday as a forecast cold snap in the coming weeks fed fears across the continent’s over depleted supply this winter and costly household bills.</p><p>The Dutch month-ahead contract – the European benchmark for gas prices over the next four weeks– rose by as much as 8.6% to €96.08, before settling up 4% at €92.50.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/23/gas-prices-in-europe-surge-as-forecast-cold-snap-feeds-supply-shortage-fears">Continue reading...</a></description>

    <item>
      <title>Monday briefing: What could Andy Burnham’s reset mean for the UK?</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/23/monday-briefing-what-could-andy-burnhams-reset-mean-for-the-uk</link>
      <description><p>In today’s newsletter: The prime minister has reopened the debate over a future relationship with a changed EU – as the bloc faces the rise of the far right, a protectionist economic agenda and growing defence ambitions</p><p>Good morning. Nobody really wants to think about Brexit any more, save for the original Brexiters, who seem delighted that Andy Burnham’s “reset” with the EU has given them an excuse to get the old gang back together. But arguments about whether the UK should rejoin the EU will reignite in parliament this week, as Burnham briefs MPs on the deal he agreed on Friday.</p><p>That deal wasn’t so much a victory as the culmination of Keir Starmer’s incrementalist approach to UK-EU relations. Its core agreements haven’t been ratified by member states yet, and the EU won’t sign them off until Britain resolves a dispute over tuition fees for European students. Burnham is apparently “determined” to take the UK back into the EU, but don’t expect any progress on that before the next general election.</p><p><em><strong>Cop</strong></em><em><strong>31 </strong></em>| The EU, the UK and allies in the developing world <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/22/cop31-climate-talks-set-to-end-in-deep-division-as-key-deal-rejected">rejected what they called an unacceptable deal</a> that “failed to meet the moment” in a dramatic finish to the UN talks in Turkey. The proposed deal failed to endorse a away from fossil fuels that more than 130 countries demanded.</p><p><em><strong>Russia </strong></em>| A Russian warship docked in the Libyan port city of Benghazi was struck in a suspected <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/22/blast-russian-ship-suspected-drone-attack-benghazi-libya">Ukrainian sea drone attack</a>, causing a dramatic night-time explosion and the sinking of the vessel.</p><p><em><strong>Weapons</strong></em>| The Red Cross and other rights groups <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/science/2026/nov/22/red-cross-warns-too-late-regulate-autonomous-weapons-united-nations">have warned that it will soon</a> be too late to properly regulate the development of autonomous weapons. The warning came as the UN Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons concluded without an agreement on an instrument for regulating autonomous weapons.</p><p><em><strong>UK news </strong></em>| Dozens of hospitals are so short of money they may not be able to continue caring for patients and are being forced to make “unpalatable” cuts to services and staff,<a href="https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026/nov/22/nhs-savings-hospitals-trusts-england-cuts"> the Guardian can reveal.</a></p><p><em><strong>West Bank </strong></em>| Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/22/netanyahu-rival-condemns-settler-arson-attacks-palestinian-villages-west-bank">condemned arson attacks</a> by militant Israeli settlers on Palestinian villages in the occupied West Bank after dozens of settlers raided Palestinian communities overnight on Saturday.</p><p><em><strong>Monday</strong></em> | FIFA is set to announce that the UK will host the 2035 Women’s World Cup.</p><p><em><strong>Thursday </strong></em>| RMT will begin a series of eight 24-hour strikes on the London Underground over the next three months due to a dispute over a four-day week for its drivers.</p><p><em><strong>Sunday</strong></em> | Spain will hold snap parliamentary elections in what will be the country’s sixth general election in 11 years.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/23/monday-briefing-what-could-andy-burnhams-reset-mean-for-the-uk">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>US intelligence chief says he trusts Trump’s description of Putin as ‘my friend’</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/22/intelligence-chief-jay-clayton-trump-putin-my-friend</link>
      <description><p>Jay Clayton was pressed on Trump’s characterization of Putin during media appearances on Sunday</p><p>Jay Clayton, the US director of national intelligence, said he trusts Donald Trump “completely” after the US president called Vladimir Putin “a friend” during <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/video/2026/nov/19/trump-greets-putin-before-holding-talks-at-apec-summit-video">their recent meeting</a> in China.</p><p>Clayton made the remarks on Sunday, where he was pressed during media appearances on Trump’s warm characterization of the Russian president – who is viewed as a chief US adversary – following his trilateral summit with Putin and China’s Xi Jinping. After a backlash at home and aboard, Trump doubled down on Saturday and <a href="https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/posts/117656427563362319">posted a photo of himself and Putin </a>shaking hands with the caption “My Friend.”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/22/intelligence-chief-jay-clayton-trump-putin-my-friend">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>After chaos at airlines, banks and companies from Microsoft to Apple, people have become convinced the world’s systems are under attack</p><p>Nicole Reindorf’s American Airlines flight was ready for takeoff in Phoenix when the pilot came on the intercom and announced what was to become the longest nationwide aviation shutdown since <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/september11">9/11</a>.</p><p>Reindorf, 70, had seen the headlines hours before about a <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/live/2026/nov/13/microsoft-outage-down-today-live-update-outlook-teams-365-when-fixed-latest-status-cause-news">global Microsoft outage</a>. She immediately suspected the two were linked in some way by AI-related threats – and that she would not get to the wedding of her best friend’s son in California.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/22/hacks-ai-internet-outages-airlines-banks-microsoft-apple">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Two weeks after Democrats flipped Congress, conservative outlets are having conversations on whether to distance themselves from Trump or double down on Maga</p><p>As a so-called “blue wave” crashed across the country on the night of 3 November, conservative hosts and commentators on Fox News <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/04/trump-blames-fox-news-republican-losses">displayed an almost virtuosic ability to avoid directly blaming Donald Trump</a> for the Republican party’s defeat, instead pinning the blame on impertinent voters who didn’t grasp the strength of the economy.</p><p>“In some sense, Mr Trump was too successful in the first year and didn’t sell it enough in the second year,” said Larry Kudlow, a Fox Business Network host who served as the president’s director of the National Economic Council during his first administration.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/22/conservative-media-trump-midterm-elections-results">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Union leaders from 19 countries urge reassessment of ties to Amazon, citing company’s poor record on worker rights</p><p>More than 30 labor union leaders from 19 countries are calling on governments to review their public contracts with Amazon and Amazon Web Services, citing the company’s poor record on worker rights and collective bargaining, in an<a href="https://uniglobalunion.org/wp-content/uploads/Amazon-procurement-letter-embargoed-until-nov-19.pdf"> open letter</a> published on Thursday.</p><p>“Amazon’s consistent record of disrespect for workers’ fundamental rights should disqualify it from being awarded public contracts – its behaviour is fundamentally inconsistent with the shared democratic values of our countries,” the union leaders wrote.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/nov/19/labor-unions-amazon-contracts-open-letter">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>A layoff and a leap of faith convinced Katie Teixeira she had what it takes to run her own business</p><p>In 2010, Katie Teixeira adopted a kitten found all alone in an abandoned house. As the cat grew, so did the connection between them.</p><p>“We just bonded,” Teixeira says. “Like mother and daughter.”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/apr/24/pet-memorial-jewelry-small-business">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>When partners consider finances, when is it ‘my’ money, and when it is ‘our’ money? Guardian readers shared their experiences </p><ul><li><a href="http://www.theguardian.com/lifeandstyle/2014/aug/08/end-loveless-marriage-financially-dependent">Private lives: ‘I want to end my marriage but I’m financially dependent</a>’<br></li></ul><p>A survey of about 1,000 Americans found that one in 10 would describe their partner as a financial bully.       <link>https://www.theguardian.com/news/2026/jan/22/gullah-geechee-georgia-development-referendum</link>
      <description><p>A citizen referendum, only the second of its kind in Georgia history, seeks to block a zoning amendment</p><p>Ire Gene Grovner stood behind his house on a recent morning, between chicken pens on one side and rows of winter collard greens on the other, holding a knife and skinning a raccoon splayed across a wood post.</p><p>“The meat is good roasted,” Grovner said. He pointed to the collards, a burst of green in the winter cold, and the chickens, with their eggs. “If you ain’t lazy, you can live good here,” he said, referring to Sapelo Island off the coast of southern <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/georgia-news">Georgia</a>.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/news/2026/jan/22/gullah-geechee-georgia-development-referendum">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/premier-league-10-talking-points-from-the-weekends-action</link>
      <description><p>Leeds offer Chelsea a lesson, Newcastle’s summer recruits struggle and Jules Ahoka makes a name for himself</p><p>What to make of Manchester United’s utterly torrid start under Mauricio Pochettino? To go glass half full as the new head coach had only three days to prepare the side for the trip to Anfield, the hope will be that time will cast the 4-0 humbling from Liverpool as the falsest of false starts. The glass-half-empty scenario, though, is that here was an XI packed with internationals that had zero clue how to sort out a dire beginning themselves. Leny Yoro’s very early red card may have been questionable but for the wall to evaporate and allow Dominik Szoboszlai’s subsequent free-kick to arrow home was damning evidence of how immature Pochettino’s new charges are. From here it became a debacle and the players, if they have anything about them, need to apologise to the head coach, hold a meeting between themselves and demand they start taking responsibility. If not, United are heading only one way: down. <strong>Jamie Jackson</strong></p><p>Match report: <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/liverpool-manchester-united-premier-league-match-report">Liverpool 4-0 Manchester United</a></p><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/mauricio-pochettino-manchester-united-reign-begins-with-anfield-humiliation-liverpool">‘It’s painful for me’: Pochettino criticises Yoro red card decision</a></p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/premier-league-10-talking-points-from-the-weekends-action">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/thierno-barry-rise-david-moyes-purring-everton</link>
      <description><p>Everton striker has worked hard to find his scoring touch after admitting he hit ‘rock bottom’ at times last season</p><p>A most unexpected name sits behind the phenomenon Erling Haaland and the £125m proven marksman Alexander Isak in the Premier League goalscoring chart this season. The rise of Thierno Barry may have surprised even the man himself but stands as a fitting reward for single-minded perseverance and the refusal to quit.</p><p>“Fabulous” was David Moyes’s take on Barry’s last performance for Everton, when <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/06/everton-coventry-premier-league-match-report">a double against Coventry</a> took the striker to 10 goals for the season in all competitions and his team temporarily up to fifth. It was high praise indeed from a manager who does not dispense tributes freely, and can appear to be on the French forward’s case constantly, but was no more than Barry deserved for a display that also featured an assist for Everton’s third goal of the night. His six Premier League goals leave him joint third alongside Evanilson of Bournemouth and Aston Villa’s Nicolas Jackson.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/thierno-barry-rise-david-moyes-purring-everton">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>New manager, new formation, familiar defensive failings. Twice Crystal Palace equalised. They seemed to have stabilised after half-time. But sometimes the rot is so deep-rooted <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/19/thomas-frank-crystal-palace-premier-league">that the new manager</a> bounce manifests as nothing more than it not looking quite as shambolic as it did before. Thomas Frank started with a defeat that means Palace remain bottom of the table having lost five league games in a row.</p><p>Yet for much of the second half, there had been reasons for Palace optimism. They seemed to have settled better after a ludicrous first half in which neither side looked at all capable of defending. But a triple substitution by Frank Lampard with 20 minutes to go shifted the game back in Coventry’s favour. With five minutes remaining, a long throw arced into the box. Brandon Thomas-Asante headed it goalwards. Dean Henderson got in the way but the ball bounced off him, hit Dwight McNeil and ricocheted in. “We came through with spirit,” Lampard said. “There was good play and a big impact from the subs. It’s a good sign for the squad.”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/coventry-crystal-palace-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Manchester City are living in Premier League purgatory, without a win in four, but at least against Fulham they ended a three-game losing run.       <title>César Azpilicueta: ‘At Chelsea a draw was a catastrophe – if you can’t perform, you’re out’</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/cesar-azpilicueta-at-chelsea-a-draw-was-a-catastrophe-if-you-cant-perform-youre-out</link>
      <description><p>Former defender reflects on his record-breaking longevity, kicking Eden Hazard in training, and life after retirement</p><p>César Azpilicueta looks well. César Azpilicueta always looks well – “ah, Captain Handsome,” one Chelsea fan says when told who’s turning up – but today especially, smiling in the sunshine. Strolling in, he eases into an easier chair, golf course spreading out beyond the terrace, west of Madrid, and orders a detox almost as green. It is nearly 20 years since he played his first game and a few months since he played his last, training kit replaced by bermudas, loafers and a polo, a picture of relaxation. So what’s it like <em>not</em> being a footballer? “Well, different,” he says. Then he laughs, which he does a lot.</p><p>It is not a laugh-your-head-off laugh, more a chuckle, a giggle, as if amused at everything he did. And for all the self-deprecation, the lack of triumphalism, he did everything. Now, at 37, it’s not the same, although there remains much to do, Azpilicueta as understated and quietly busy as ever: “square,” he calls himself. He’s completed an MBA, a sports directorship diploma and there are media offers, a life to live. Matches to play still: against his kids the needle is never far away, he says. And although he hasn’t found a seven-a-side team yet he will.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/cesar-azpilicueta-at-chelsea-a-draw-was-a-catastrophe-if-you-cant-perform-youre-out">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Training hard and biding his time, Dele Alli has not given up on football yet</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/20/dele-alli-tottenham-mk-dons-england</link>
      <description><p>The 30-year-old former England star combines Twitch streaming with working to return to the top as a player</p><p>Consider the training regime Dele Alli has followed since he left Como 18 months ago and it becomes clear why he takes exception to suggestions he has given up on football in favour of becoming an internet personality.</p><p>He trains five or six days a week with Connor Peters, an elite performance coach who has worked with players including Trevoh Chalobah. They spend four days on the pitch and days in between in the gym. A typical day begins at 9am with an hour of activation and stretching before Dele heads to non-league Windsor &amp; Eton at 11am, where he trains on the pitches and uses the facilities. Then it’s back home to use his own oxygen chamber and sauna for a recovery session.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/20/dele-alli-tottenham-mk-dons-england">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Gonzalo García: ‘I love Craven Cottage – the fans can reach out and touch you’</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/19/gonzalo-garcia-fulham-spain-premier-leaue-interview</link>
      <description><p>Spain Under-21 striker admits the pace of the Premier League has surprised him but says he must stay calm over goal drought at Fulham</p><p>The first thing Rita Hayworth’s great nephew says when he walks in is: “Sorry I’m late.” Gonzalo García is not late, but it’s very like him: he is impeccably polite, accommodating, and there’s an almost gentle quality to him, a calm that’s not common but can help, especially in moments when the pressure builds. There’s a reason one of the coaches standing in the rain by the pitch where Spain’s under‑21s have just finished training says everyone here loves García. The Fulham striker shakes hands, introduces himself and ducks into the dressing room to change; then a few minutes later he’s back, apologising for a wait that wasn’t one.</p><p>Time to talk, so let’s start with Tinseltown, the family tale. García laughs. His great-aunt, born Margarita Carmen Cansino, was among the biggest stars in Hollywood, although he’s not sure he’s seen any of her films. His grandfather was a surgeon and others in the family followed. His uncles played rugby for Spain, but that wasn’t his thing. As for him, he enrolled in a degree in business management and analytics, and reckons he might have liked law, yet even that wasn’t his chosen field.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/19/gonzalo-garcia-fulham-spain-premier-leaue-interview">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>‘Fragile’ Chelsea must toughen up after Leeds humiliation, admits Xabi Alonso</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/chelsea-leeds-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p></p><p>Xabi Alonso is straying towards crisis territory. Here’s a mind-bending statistic: Chelsea are eighth but have now lost more league games than Manchester United. They were bullied by a rampant Leeds United, who fully merited their first win at Stamford Bridge since going top with a 2-0 victory in December 1999, and can look forward to another season with no European football if they do not sharpen up soon.</p><p>It is not really worth dwelling on the fact that the second Leeds goal, a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty converted early in an astonishingly one-sided second half, came after Morgan Rogers was harshly penalised for handball. That was a minor detail given the wider picture. Leeds, superbly coached by Daniel Farke and up to sixth after two clinical strikes from Noah Okafor, Calvert-Lewin’s sixth goal of the season and a late effort from Brenden Aaronson, were so dominant that they had no real need for a helping hand from the officials.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/chelsea-leeds-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Aston Villa held at home as dogged Sunderland battle for Régis Le Bris</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/aston-villa-sunderland-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p>For <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/aston-villa">Aston Villa</a>, a painful stalemate at home to Sunderland, but for Régis Le Bris and his players, this was another triumph of sorts. The raw numbers spoke volumes of Villa’s struggles against a defence that backed themselves to keep Unai Emery’s side at bay. All but one of Villa’s seven shots on target came from outside the visitors’ box and the one inside it, courtesy of Ian Maatsen, was forgettable. Owing to a summer of change, injuries and Emery resting John McGinn with Tuesday’s game at Galatasaray in mind, Maatsen, incredibly, was the sole survivor in the Villa starting XI from when these sides played out a 4-3 classic seven months ago.</p><p>Villa were too predictable, short of a spark, someone to unpick an organised back line. Johan Manzambi, Emi Buendía and Alysson all flattered to deceive on an afternoon when Ibrahim Mbaye and McGinn arrived from the bench. Alejandro Garnacho, however, was not involved in Villa’s matchday squad for the second successive match and the Chelsea loanee has played just 38 minutes in the Premier League this campaign. Tammy Abraham, the match-winner in April, was also left out and a January move looks likely.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/aston-villa-sunderland-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

French teenagers on Tuesday clashed with police as they kept up a blockade of high schools in cities across the country to demand better conditions and more teacher hirings. The escalating standoff came as unions staged a day of demonstrations against a cost-cutting budget drafted by Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu's embattled government.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/560db0a6-bc0e-11f1-a13f-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/07e46c53e327acb7cdaffe512bca997cd100349d.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/560db0a6-bc0e-11f1-a13f-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/07e46c53e327acb7cdaffe512bca997cd100349d.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b23ed102-bbeb-11f1-861d-cf265369200f</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:53:59 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/560db0a6-bc0e-11f1-a13f-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/07e46c53e327acb7cdaffe512bca997cd100349d.jpg">© Sameer Al-Doumy, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Legion of Honour: Police investigate corruption claims for France’s top award</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-legion-of-honour-police-investigate-corruption-claims-for-france-s-top-award</link><description>
French police took a top general into custody last week as part of an ongoing probe into potential bribery among the selection committee for the country’s highest decoration, the Legion of Honour. Investigations centre on possible payoffs for awards including expensive meals, holidays and thousands of euros in cash.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">cf7e5750-bc0f-11f1-9d67-9d40f7c16032</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 14:43:40 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg">© Francois Mori, AP</source><dc:creator>Joanna YORK</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Eiffel Tower chief to step down over removal of women staff during Hindu group's visit</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-eiffel-tower-chief-to-step-down-over-removal-of-women-staff-during-hindu-group-visit-baps</link><description>
The head of the Eiffel Tower is set to step down in the wake of a controversy sparked by the removal of female workers during a private visit of the Paris landmark by members of the Hindu sect BAPS, which triggered a staff walkout earlier this month and sparked outrage in France.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b85f821e-bc10-11f1-89fe-7b0f1abdd3bc</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 14:22:29 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg">© Kenzo Tribouillard, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France's Le Pen vows to 'counterattack' after top ally Bardella hit by anti-Semitism claims</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-france-s-le-pen-vows-to-counterattack-after-top-ally-bardella-hit-by-anti-semitism-claims</link><description>
French presidential frontrunner Marine Le Pen on Tuesday denounced an attempt to "derail" her Élysée Palace run after a media report accused the head of her far-right National Rally (RN) party, Jordan Bardella, of making ant-Semitic comments in 2013. Le Pen said Bardella, who is tipped to be prime minister if she wins the presidency, had her "total confidence".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0b97a704-bc02-11f1-8bbb-ad34ceb9e2f1</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 12:33:58 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg">© Anne-Christine Poujoulat, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France puts out massive fire that torched 42,000 hectares and smouldered for 69 days</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260928-france-puts-out-massive-fire-that-torched-42-000-hectares-and-smouldered-for-69-days</link><description>
France's largest wildfire since 1949 has been declared extinguished more than two months after it broke out in southwestern Gironde, forcing the evacuation of around 224,000 people and covering the city of Bordeaux with a thick plume of smoke. The blaze was put under control on August 1, but continued to smoulder underground for weeks.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0f68114c-bb5e-11f1-a5f5-19c8c18b5c0d</guid><pubDate>Mon, 28 Sep 2026 17:00:08 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg">© Julien De Rosa, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Far-right politician Éric Zemmour joins 2027 French presidential race</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-far-right-politician-%C3%A9ric-zemmour-joins-2027-french-presidential-race</link><description>
French far-right politician Éric Zemmour said on Friday that he would run in next year's presidential election, joining far-right candidate Marine Le Pen, who was runner-up to President Emmanuel Macron in the last two elections. Zemmour is campaigning on a crackdown on immigration, including a plan to expel unemployed foreigners even if they are legal residents. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2e6bcd08-b33a-11f1-b960-e76b244d1c83</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:06:31 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg">© Emma Da Silva, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French PM vows to cut public spending by €54 billion to reduce deficit</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-french-pm-vows-to-cut-public-spending-by-%E2%82%AC54-billion-to-reduce-deficit</link><description>
Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said on Thursday that France will cut public spending by €54 billion next year to reduce the country's deficit. The announcement comes seven months ahead of the country's presidential election, and the government is wary of a new wave of demonstrations with a jump in global oil prices sparking concerns over the rising cost of living. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">61b975d6-b32e-11f1-ab9e-b5bbc83805db</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 07:23:41 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg">© Ludovic Marin, AFP via AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

The latest information, news and events in France, Europe and around the world.</description><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/</link><lastBuildDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 08:48:59 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>France</category><title>French right backs Macron's plan to put public spending limits in Constitution</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261122-french-right-backs-macron-s-plan-to-put-public-spending-limits-in-constitution</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron is reportedly considering a constitutional reform to curb public deficits, with right-wing parties and the far-right National Rally signalling their willingness to support the move. The proposal could bring MPs and senators together for a vote as early as January, just months before the 2027 presidential election.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/445a5ffc-e662-11f1-8900-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/000-36LK6NK-1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/445a5ffc-e662-11f1-8900-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/000-36LK6NK-1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">4bea9e76-e66c-11f1-b8f3-f96315fbf1b4</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 18:09:18 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/445a5ffc-e662-11f1-8900-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/000-36LK6NK-1.jpg">AFP - STEPHANIE LECOCQ</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Students and unions unite for sixth weekend of protests across France</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261121-students-and-unions-unite-for-sixth-weekend-of-protests-across-france</link><description>
Thousands of demonstrators took to the streets across France on Saturday for a sixth consecutive weekend of protests against rising living costs, deteriorating public services and growing inequality. The movement, which began with student demonstrations in September, has since broadened into a nationwide campaign and inspired similar rallies elsewhere in Europe.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/1a778cb4-e5b3-11f1-a8b6-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D88M7VC.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/1a778cb4-e5b3-11f1-a8b6-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D88M7VC.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">7ad79414-e5c2-11f1-8bc6-7d93519529c2</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 16:43:57 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/1a778cb4-e5b3-11f1-a8b6-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D88M7VC.jpg">AFP - GUILLAUME SALIGOT</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French court finds racism played role in police beating of black music producer</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261121-french-court-finds-racism-played-role-in-police-beating-of-black-music-producer</link><description>
A French court has handed down prison sentences to three police officers for the violent assault of black music producer Michel Zecler in Paris in 2020, ruling that racism was an aggravating factor in a case that sparked nationwide outrage over police brutality and racial discrimination.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/17c071ac-e4f5-11f1-9df3-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-20T101436Z-2082553690-RC2LROA9VG3U-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-JUSTICE-ZECLER.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/17c071ac-e4f5-11f1-9df3-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-20T101436Z-2082553690-RC2LROA9VG3U-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-JUSTICE-ZECLER.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">eadc87ac-e58a-11f1-b7fe-efd3e07e368d</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 15:41:58 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/17c071ac-e4f5-11f1-9df3-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-20T101436Z-2082553690-RC2LROA9VG3U-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-JUSTICE-ZECLER.jpg">REUTERS - Benoit Tessier</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>National Assembly backs greater legal protection for police using firearms</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261121-national-assembly-backs-greater-legal-protection-for-police-using-firearms</link><description>
France's parliament has approved legislation giving police officers greater legal protection when using their firearms, prompting fierce criticism from rights groups who warn it could make it harder to investigate alleged police brutality. The government insists the measure is needed to protect officers carrying out increasingly demanding duties.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/07ce511e-d53d-11f1-ab78-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-31T142906Z-217842348-RC2CEOAPZ05N-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/07ce511e-d53d-11f1-ab78-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-31T142906Z-217842348-RC2CEOAPZ05N-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">a15be40c-e589-11f1-9ce2-a7af964aafae</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 13:44:03 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/07ce511e-d53d-11f1-ab78-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-31T142906Z-217842348-RC2CEOAPZ05N-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">REUTERS - Nicolas Economou</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Former PM de Villepin launches 2027 presidential bid with warning to far right</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261121-former-pm-de-villepin-launches-20207-presidential-bid-with-warning-to-far-right</link><description>
Former French prime minister Dominique de Villepin has announced his candidacy for the 2027 presidential election, promising to restore France's international influence, tackle growing inequality and challenge the rise of the far right. The veteran conservative also delivered a blistering assessment of President Emmanuel Macron's leadership, accusing him of allowing the country's political and social divisions to deepen.

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bed8c53e-0bda-11f0-8024-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/2025-03-24T122520Z_62888456_RC2OJDAL4NRJ_RTRMADP_3_PEOPLE-DEPARDIEU-TRIAL.JPG"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bed8c53e-0bda-11f0-8024-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/2025-03-24T122520Z_62888456_RC2OJDAL4NRJ_RTRMADP_3_PEOPLE-DEPARDIEU-TRIAL.JPG" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">514af00c-e1a1-11f1-82bc-0f0371ba9765</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:19:17 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bed8c53e-0bda-11f0-8024-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/2025-03-24T122520Z_62888456_RC2OJDAL4NRJ_RTRMADP_3_PEOPLE-DEPARDIEU-TRIAL.JPG">REUTERS - Benoit Tessier</source><dc:creator>Paul Myers</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French cybercrime unit probes massive cyberattack on La Poste subsidiary</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261116-french-cybercrime-unit-probes-massive-cyberattack-on-la-poste-subsidiary</link><description>
A French anti-cybercrime unit was on Monday investigating a massive cyberattack which targeted a subsidiary of the La Poste group mid-September. The contact details of 22 million people were exposed during the attack, the Paris prosecutor's office confirmed on Sunday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/9c15b61e-7f67-11f0-b513-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/2018-08-30t091729z-276704098-rc1fe83a8590-rtrmadp-3-france-insurance-merger-0.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/9c15b61e-7f67-11f0-b513-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/2018-08-30t091729z-276704098-rc1fe83a8590-rtrmadp-3-france-insurance-merger-0.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f7093a68-e114-11f1-aa3b-e18acb043b04</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 07:01:47 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/9c15b61e-7f67-11f0-b513-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/2018-08-30t091729z-276704098-rc1fe83a8590-rtrmadp-3-france-insurance-merger-0.jpg">REUTERS - ERIC GAILLARD</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Harki families take legal action over children's 'ghost graves' in France</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261115-harki-families-take-legal-action-over-children-s-ghost-graves-in-france</link><description>

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/d71114e0-dd33-11f1-ac87-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/000-32476WP.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/d71114e0-dd33-11f1-ac87-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/000-32476WP.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">cb9c44a8-dded-11f1-9b62-d30335cd8455</guid><pubDate>Sun, 15 Nov 2026 15:07:27 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/d71114e0-dd33-11f1-ac87-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/000-32476WP.jpg">© Pascal Guyot / AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Women in France report painful periods after exposure to tear gas at protests</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261115-women-in-france-report-painful-periods-after-exposure-to-tear-gas-at-protests</link><description>
Thousands of women in France have reported unusually painful periods, heavy bleeding and disrupted menstrual cycles after being exposed to tear gas during the country's recent protests, prompting calls for an investigation into its possible effects on reproductive health.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/12979562-ddd8-11f1-83db-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T134903Z-250942565-RC2PHOAN2E2K-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/12979562-ddd8-11f1-83db-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T134903Z-250942565-RC2PHOAN2E2K-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">5343e1a8-dd22-11f1-9ec6-3535b33525c6</guid><pubDate>Sun, 15 Nov 2026 10:14:03 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/12979562-ddd8-11f1-83db-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T134903Z-250942565-RC2PHOAN2E2K-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">REUTERS - Stephane Mahe</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

La date du verdict du TAS enfin connue</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/sports/20261123-can-2025-maroc-senegal-verdict-tas</link><description>
Face à l'impatience concernant le litige entre le Sénégal et le Maroc et le titre de champion d'Afrique 2025, le Tribunal arbitral du sport (TAS) de Lausanne est sorti de son silence lundi. Il a annoncé la date de son verdict.

L’Olympique de Marseille s’est incliné à domicile face au Mans (3-2). Alors qu’il menait 2-0 après 40 minutes et des buts de Gouiri (33’) et Paixão (40’), l’OM s’est écroulé.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/659a3e8c-e6e2-11f1-a088-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/om-1-2.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/659a3e8c-e6e2-11f1-a088-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/om-1-2.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">8b865d4c-e6e2-11f1-a878-2fb0ef8e8037</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 07:30:26 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>L'Equipe TV</dc:creator></item><item><category>Dans la presse</category><title>COP31, le flop</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/dans-la-presse/20261123-cop31-le-flop</link><description>
À la une de la presse, ce lundi 23 novembre, l’échec de la COP31 à cause, notamment, de référence aux énergies fossiles, dans la proposition finale. Le choc, en Italie, après le suicide d’un ancien chef de la police, retrouvé mort, samedi, à son domicile. Les témoignages des sœurs de Pengo Bossio Wangi, victime d’un assassinat raciste à Trappes, en banlieue parisienne, il y a un mois jour pour jour. Et une découverte qui va peut-être nous éclairer un peu plus sur nos origines.

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/7c6acbcc-e68d-11f1-82fb-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-141656-142707-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/7c6acbcc-e68d-11f1-82fb-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-141656-142707-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">81e42472-e68d-11f1-bdc9-97845bc94794</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 16:38:38 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Climat : la COP31 échoue devant la division des pays sur les énergies fossiles</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261122-climat-la-cop31-%C3%A9choue-devant-la-division-des-pays-sur-les-%C3%A9nergies-fossiles</link><description>
La COP31, la plus longue conférence de l'ONU sur le climat de l'histoire, s'est terminée sur un échec ce dimanche 22 novembre à Antalya en Turquie, après le rejet par l'Union européenne et d'autres pays d'un projet de décision finale omettant les énergies fossiles.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2b2b3502-e68e-11f1-ba46-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-160141-160331-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2b2b3502-e68e-11f1-ba46-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-160141-160331-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">3039e6c4-e68e-11f1-bd13-c3178e8c146c</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 16:37:45 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>COP31 à Antalya : pas d'accord en vue ?</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261122-cop31-%C3%A0-antalya-pas-d-accord-en-vue</link><description>
La COP31 à Antalya est déjà la COP la plus longue de l’histoire, avec 44 heures de prolongations. Les négociations s’enlisent sur les énergies fossiles. Nous en parlons avec notre correspondante Jenna Le Bras.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/7a9cca28-e68f-11f1-80c8-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-120103-120442-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/7a9cca28-e68f-11f1-80c8-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-120103-120442-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">7fc9d680-e68f-11f1-889c-a757f882d559</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 16:35:32 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>COP31 à Antalya : la plus longue COP de l'histoire s'achève sur un échec</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261122-cop31-%C3%A0-antalya-la-plus-longue-cop-de-l-histoire-s-ach%C3%A8ve-sur-un-%C3%A9chec</link><description>
La COP31, la plus longue conférence de l'ONU sur le climat de l'histoire, s'est terminée sur un échec dimanche 22 novembre à Antalya, en Turquie, après le rejet par l'Union européenne et d'autres pays d'un projet de décision finale omettant les énergies fossiles. "On ressent de la déception et beaucoup de colère, parce que ce scénario aurait pu être évité", rapporte notre invitée Marine Pouget, responsable de la gouvernance internationale sur le climat au sein du Réseau Action Climat.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a88dc460-e68e-11f1-8b4d-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-160332-160953-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a88dc460-e68e-11f1-8b4d-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-160332-160953-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ad688a2e-e68e-11f1-92ab-cdddf46835ec</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 16:35:25 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Échec de la COP31 à Antalya : "Nous sommes passés à côté d'une opportunité"</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261122-%C3%A9chec-de-la-cop31-%C3%A0-antalya-nous-sommes-pass%C3%A9s-%C3%A0-c%C3%B4t%C3%A9-d-une-opportunit%C3%A9</link><description>
"Nous sommes passés à côté d'une opportunité", a reconnu le président de la COP après de très longues négociations. La COP31 à Antalya se termine donc sur un échec. Nous en parlons avec notre invitée Charlotte Chaussat, cofondatrice de la Coordination Climat. "Cette COP se passait dans un climat compliqué", rappelle-t-elle.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/c43d5b72-e665-11f1-a6c8-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-22T095903Z-917320092-RC2XSOA2A529-RTRMADP-3-CLIMATE-COP31.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/c43d5b72-e665-11f1-a6c8-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-22T095903Z-917320092-RC2XSOA2A529-RTRMADP-3-CLIMATE-COP31.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">51a71434-e68f-11f1-a222-df3693cae406</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 16:34:17 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>COP31 : décryptage après son échec malgré 44 heures de prolongations</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261122-cop31-d%C3%A9cryptage-apr%C3%A8s-son-%C3%A9chec-malgr%C3%A9-44-heures-de-prolongations</link><description>
La COP31 à Antalya se solde par un échec. Nous en parlons avec notre chroniqueuse Anne Corpet. "À la COP, les décisions se prennent par consensus : il faut l'unanimité. Le constat, c’est que l’alliance des pays hostiles à toute avancée a été plus forte que celle de ceux qui souhaitent avancer sur le plan climatique", explique-t-elle.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/48155c68-e690-11f1-ab2c-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-170326-170857-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/48155c68-e690-11f1-ab2c-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-170326-170857-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">4d3f6274-e690-11f1-84d0-cff2360bfc82</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 16:30:55 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

Il n'y aura pas d'avion dans le ciel belge ce lundi 23 novembre : c'est la conséquence d'une grève nationale contre la vie chère. Alors que le gouvernement fédéral belge cherche difficilement à négocier un budget de rigueur qui vise à économiser 10 milliards d'euros au cours des prochaines années, les syndicats ont appelé à faire front commun et à une « grande mobilisation citoyenne » pour dénoncer la politique d’austérité ainsi que la baisse du pouvoir d’achat. Une journée à laquelle ont décidé de se joindre les contrôleurs aériens, ce qui va entièrement paralyser le trafic des avions toute la journée. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/30485b52-1aa4-11f1-a9dc-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25330424076154.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/30485b52-1aa4-11f1-a9dc-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25330424076154.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2b34cece-e719-11f1-9a3f-47fc1c531e42</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:00:21 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/30485b52-1aa4-11f1-a9dc-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25330424076154.jpg">© Mark Carlson / AP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Hongrie: la détention provisoire d'un ancien ministre d'Orban dans une enquête de corruption prolongée</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261123-hongrie-la-d%C3%A9tention-provisoire-d-un-ancien-ministre-d-orban-dans-une-enqu%C3%AAte-de-corruption-prolong%C3%A9e</link><description>
En Hongrie, Miklos Sesztak, l’ancien ministre du Développement national entre 2014 et 2018, et actuel député au Parlement hongrois, a été arrêté fin septembre. Il est soupçonné d’avoir détourné de l’argent public et d’avoir touché d’énormes pots-de-vin. Lors d’une perquisition à son domicile, la police a trouvé plusieurs coffres-forts vides. Il y a huit jours, les autorités hongroises découvraient un immense butin : près de 16 millions d’euros en liquide, cachés dans des forêts, des granges et des entrepôts. La détention provisoire de Miklos Sesztak a été prolongée jusqu’à fin janvier. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/023295d4-23b4-11f1-9c2f-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-03-19T090058Z-1009523912-RC2K7KA3JXOS-RTRMADP-3-IRAN-CRISIS-EU-SUMMIT.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/023295d4-23b4-11f1-9c2f-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-03-19T090058Z-1009523912-RC2K7KA3JXOS-RTRMADP-3-IRAN-CRISIS-EU-SUMMIT.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">c47e8f4c-e715-11f1-a7a3-277926f246bd</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 08:23:57 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/023295d4-23b4-11f1-9c2f-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-03-19T090058Z-1009523912-RC2K7KA3JXOS-RTRMADP-3-IRAN-CRISIS-EU-SUMMIT.jpg">REUTERS - Yves Herman</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Le grand invité international</category><title>Sylvie Bermann: «Les Européens sont impuissants face aux actes hostiles russes»</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/le-grand-invit%C3%A9-international/20261123-sylvie-bermann-les-europ%C3%A9ens-sont-impuissants-face-aux-actes-hostiles-russes</link><description>

C'est une affaire de « veuves noires » qui choque la Russie : dans la région de Volgograd, neuf personnes sont accusées d'avoir organisé un réseau pour récupérer les primes de militaires blessés ou tués en Ukraine, grâce à des mariages fictifs conclus avant l'engagement des soldats dans l'armée. </description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/c4918b74-e50d-11f1-94fe-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/GettyImages-2306076594.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/c4918b74-e50d-11f1-94fe-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/GettyImages-2306076594.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">1853515c-e50e-11f1-8321-3bce4db5bc5f</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 18:25:27 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/c4918b74-e50d-11f1-94fe-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/GettyImages-2306076594.jpg">© Massimiliano Donati / Getty Images</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Le Danemark accuse la Russie d'avoir tenté d'assassiner un rappeur ukrainien</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261120-le-danemark-va-expulser-un-diplomate-russe-apr%C3%A8s-la-tentative-d-assassinat-d-un-ukrainien-sur-son-sol</link><description>
Le Danemark va expulser l'attaché de défense de l'ambassade de Russie après la tentative d'assassinat d'un rappeur ukrainien sur son sol, qu'il soupçonne Moscou d'avoir orchestré, a indiqué vendredi 20 novembre le ministre danois des Affaires étrangères. La diplomatie russe a promis de riposter. « Moscou donnera une réponse appropriée », a indiqué la porte-parole du ministère russe des Affaires étrangères, Maria Zakharova, citée par l'agence de presse TASS.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/449d07e6-e507-11f1-8364-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D86T2RT.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/449d07e6-e507-11f1-8364-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D86T2RT.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">7863937e-e507-11f1-99b0-bbfd8e7adaf9</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 17:35:50 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/449d07e6-e507-11f1-8364-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D86T2RT.jpg">AFP - EMIL HELMS</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Invité international</category><title>Manifestations en Europe: «Une volonté de converger au niveau transnational et avec d'autres générations»</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/invit%C3%A9-international/20261120-manifestations-en-europe-une-volont%C3%A9-de-converger-au-niveau-transnational-et-avec-d-autres-g%C3%A9n%C3%A9rations</link><description>
La mobilisation contre la vie chère traverse toute l'Europe : des millions de personnes sont attendues dans les rues contre la vie chère et pour le droit au logement. Ce mouvement de fond, lancé à partir de ce vendredi 20 novembre, traduit des réalités communes. Ces luttes peuvent-elles vraiment converger ? Quels modes d'action pour quelles revendications ? L’analyse du sociologue Paolo Stuppia, enseignant à Sciences Po Paris et co-auteur de Géopolitique de la jeunesse – Engagement et (dé)mobilisations, publiée aux éditions Cavalier bleu.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/9142dd72-e4f9-11f1-8056-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324446135271.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/9142dd72-e4f9-11f1-8056-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324446135271.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">a69a8ac8-e4f2-11f1-a69d-dfb7bbed3c72</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:07:55 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Candice Mazaud-Tomazic</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>À la Une: Aleksandar Čupić, le sage à la tête du Parlement serbe</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261120-%C3%A0-la-une-aleksandar-%C4%8Dupi%C4%87-le-sage-%C3%A0-la-t%C3%AAte-du-parlement-serbe</link><description>
Une revue de presse des Balkans en partenariat avec Le Courrier des Balkans.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a7f28112-e4f4-11f1-85e4-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-19T152302Z-275612966-RC22ROAP2GDQ-RTRMADP-3-SERBIA-PARLIAMENT.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a7f28112-e4f4-11f1-85e4-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-19T152302Z-275612966-RC22ROAP2GDQ-RTRMADP-3-SERBIA-PARLIAMENT.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">eb8a088e-e4f2-11f1-8ab1-dffd4ffb6f91</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:41:30 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a7f28112-e4f4-11f1-85e4-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-19T152302Z-275612966-RC22ROAP2GDQ-RTRMADP-3-SERBIA-PARLIAMENT.jpg">© Djordje Kojadinovic / Reuters</source><dc:creator>Courrier des Balkans</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>UE/Royaume-Uni: Andy Burnham annonce une «réflexion» en 2027 sur les relations à long terme</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261120-ue-royaume-uni-andy-burnham-annonce-une-r%C3%A9flexion-en-2027-sur-les-relations-%C3%A0-long-terme</link><description>
Pour son premier sommet avec l’UE, le Premier ministre britannique Andy Burnham peut s’estimer satisfait. Européens et Britanniques se sont mis d’accord sur trois dossiers concernant les jeunes, les émissions de CO2 et les normes alimentaires. La « remise à zéro » imaginée par son prédécesseur Keir Starmer pour les relations entre Londres et Bruxelles est désormais sur des rails, même si union douanière, libre-circulation et marché unique restent des lignes rouges pour les Britanniques. Les Européens affirment avoir tourné la page du Brexit et se satisfont ouvertement des accords ponctuels comme ceux qui ont été trouvés ce vendredi 20 novembre.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/cfd3cb76-e4f1-11f1-a528-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324496448442.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/cfd3cb76-e4f1-11f1-a528-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324496448442.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f35856f6-e4f2-11f1-85c2-81e9611d4583</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:30:12 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/cfd3cb76-e4f1-11f1-a528-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324496448442.jpg">AP Photo/Marius Burgelman - Marius Burgelman</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Deux missiles russes tombent en Pologne, Varsovie dénonce «une provocation»</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261120-deux-missiles-russes-tombent-en-pologne-varsovie-d%C3%A9nonce-une-provocation</link><description>
Des missiles russes sont tombés ce vendredi 20 novembre 2026 en Pologne, non loin de la frontière ukrainienne, suscitant de vives réactions de Varsovie, de l'Otan, de l'Union européenne et du Royaume-Uni, tous alliés de Kiev. Le secrétaire général de l'Otan, Mark Rutte, se rendra à Varsovie samedi.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/ac76e586-e4f2-11f1-826c-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-20T091417Z-724863669-RC2KROAVQTVB-RTRMADP-3-UKRAINE-CRISIS-POLAND-OBJECTS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/ac76e586-e4f2-11f1-826c-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-20T091417Z-724863669-RC2KROAVQTVB-RTRMADP-3-UKRAINE-CRISIS-POLAND-OBJECTS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b07d5818-e4f2-11f1-be00-dfb7bbed3c72</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:02:44 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/ac76e586-e4f2-11f1-826c-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-20T091417Z-724863669-RC2KROAVQTVB-RTRMADP-3-UKRAINE-CRISIS-POLAND-OBJECTS.jpg">© Kacper Pempel / Reuters</source><dc:creator>RFI avec AFP</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Frappes russes sur Kiev: la France réclame une réunion du Conseil de sécurité de l'ONU</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261120-frappes-russes-sur-kiev-la-france-r%C3%A9clame-une-r%C3%A9union-du-conseil-de-s%C3%A9curit%C3%A9-de-l-onu</link><description>
Après la nuit de frappes russes sur Kiev en Ukraine, la France a demandé une réunion du Conseil de sécurité de l’ONU. Le ministre français de l'Europe et ⁠des Affaires étrangères, Jean-Noël Barrot, a dénoncé sur X des « crimes » et évoque des civils tués et deux ambassades touchées, celles de l’Autriche et des Pays-Bas.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a49ca4d6-be64-11f1-98b5-dd51fcab6130/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C9WK9TP.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a49ca4d6-be64-11f1-98b5-dd51fcab6130/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C9WK9TP.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">d3d92362-e4db-11f1-9258-7b676b79acdc</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 12:43:24 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a49ca4d6-be64-11f1-98b5-dd51fcab6130/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C9WK9TP.jpg">AFP - LUDOVIC MARIN</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Espagne: lors d'un débat tendu avec Alberto Nuñez Feijoo, Pedro Sanchez reconnaît des «erreurs»</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261120-espagne-lors-d-un-d%C3%A9bat-tendu-avec-alberto-nu%C3%B1ez-feijoo-pedro-sanchez-reconna%C3%AEt-des-erreurs</link><description>
Le Premier ministre socialiste espagnol Pedro Sanchez a reconnu jeudi 19 novembre des « erreurs » lors d'un face-à-face tendu face à son rival conservateur Alberto Nuñez Feijoo, qui l'a accusé d'avoir « laminé la classe moyenne » et lui a reproché son « irresponsabilité » en matière migratoire, à dix jours des législatives. La majorité des sondages donnent le Parti populaire (PP) d'Alberto Nuñez Feijoo vainqueur du scrutin du 29 novembre, mais sans majorité absolue. Pour gouverner, il pourrait s'appuyer sur la formation d'extrême droite Vox, déjà son allié dans plusieurs régions.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b78410ce-e4c6-11f1-a2aa-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26323746593101.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b78410ce-e4c6-11f1-a2aa-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26323746593101.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">58ed1d06-e4c8-11f1-a63c-9b74e97ddf48</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:12:24 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b78410ce-e4c6-11f1-a2aa-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26323746593101.jpg">© Manu Fernandez / AP</source><dc:creator>RFI avec AFP</dc:creator></item><item><category>Appels sur l'actualité</category><title>Pont de Kertch : comment l’Ukraine perturbe-t-elle l'accès à la Crimée?</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/appels-sur-l-actualit%C3%A9/20261120-pont-de-kertch-comment-l-ukraine-perturbe-t-elle-l-acc%C3%A8s-%C3%A0-la-crim%C3%A9e</link><description>
Trois frappes en quelques jours contre le pont de Kertch. L'Ukraine a de nouveau visé ce jeudi cet ouvrage stratégique qui relie la Russie à la Crimée annexée. Cette fois, c'est la partie ferroviaire qui a été touchée. Mardi déjà, une partie de la chaussée s'était effondrée, entraînant la fermeture de la circulation routière. Derrière ces frappes, un objectif : compliquer les déplacements des Russes en Crimée. Comment l'armée ukrainienne a-t-elle organisé ces attaques ? Dans quelle mesure peuvent-elles fragiliser le ravitaillement militaire sur le front ukrainien ?
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/9b8b7aa4-e284-11f1-83dd-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/Russie-Ukraine-Kertch-Info-Verif.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/9b8b7aa4-e284-11f1-83dd-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/Russie-Ukraine-Kertch-Info-Verif.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ad568480-e41f-11f1-99da-0db31b1ab018</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:05:23 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Juan Gomez</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

<rss version="2.0" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" xmlns:media="http://search.yahoo.com/mrss/" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/"><channel><language>fr</language><title>France : News et actualité en continu - France 24</title><description>France 24  couvre les évènements en France et en Outre-mer : politique, culture, faits de société, énergie, crise sociale, sport, santé, avec ses reportages, enquêtes, débats et analyses.</description><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/</link><lastBuildDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:23:42 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/fr/france/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>Au cœur de l’info, l’invité</category><title>Caroline Toby : "sans vidéosurveillance, Michel Zecler aurait été victime d'une erreur judiciaire"</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/au-c%C5%93ur-de-l-info-l-invit%C3%A9/20261122-caroline-toby-sans-vid%C3%A9osurveillance-michel-zecler-aurait-%C3%A9t%C3%A9-victime-d-une-erreur-judiciaire</link><description>
Le producteur Michel Zecler avait été passé à tabac en 2020 par trois policiers dans l'entrée de son studio d'enregistrement à Paris. Les policiers avaient établi un faux procès-verbal l'accusant de violences; or les images de vidéosurveillance avaient invalidé leur version. Les policiers viennent d'être condamnés à de la prison ferme, avec interdiction d'exercer leur métier. Le caractère raciste de ces violences a aussi été reconnu. Interview de Caroline Toby, avocate de Michel Zecler.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/912ca82c-e6ac-11f1-a33d-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-201335-202201-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/912ca82c-e6ac-11f1-a33d-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-201335-202201-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">88d84f80-e6b3-11f1-a209-c955afc4fa26</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 20:30:18 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Achren VERDIAN</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Choose France : les entreprises françaises prêtes à investir 42,5 milliards d'euros</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261122-choose-france-entreprises-fran%C3%A7aises-pr%C3%AAtent-investir-42-5-milliards-euros-emmanuel-macron-%C3%A9conomie-investissements-projet</link><description>
Les entreprises tricolores projettent d'investir 42,5 milliards d'euros en France lors du sommet Choose France qui se déroulera lundi, a détaillé l'Élysée dimanche soir. Malgré une situation économique compliquée dans le pays, plus de 200 projets industriels français seront mis à l'honneur.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0b2fc994-e6ab-11f1-9ffc-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26152618587040.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0b2fc994-e6ab-11f1-9ffc-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26152618587040.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">19c1b856-e6af-11f1-a7d0-d531a8636e90</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 19:58:34 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0b2fc994-e6ab-11f1-9ffc-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26152618587040.jpg">© Gonzalo Fuentes, Pool Reuters</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Budget : Macron confirme qu'il envisage d'inscrire une "règle d'or" dans la Constitution</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261122-budget-macron-confirme-qu-il-envisage-d-inscrire-une-r%C3%A8gle-d-or-dans-la-constitution</link><description>
Emmanuel Macron a confirmé au Figaro qu'il envisageait de faire inscrire dans la Constitution une "règle d'or" budgétaire. Un projet qui lui permettrait de quitter l'Élysée sur une mesure emblématique, rassurante pour les marchés, alors que le président est très critiqué pour sa gestion des finances publiques.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/68d14446-e512-11f1-9a4d-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/2ff1671046ae8d7a3a4d622f0cfc02f630e7ae1c.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/68d14446-e512-11f1-9a4d-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/2ff1671046ae8d7a3a4d622f0cfc02f630e7ae1c.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">fea875f4-e68c-11f1-a08c-6963c92ef58d</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 15:54:26 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/68d14446-e512-11f1-9a4d-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/2ff1671046ae8d7a3a4d622f0cfc02f630e7ae1c.jpg">© Aurelien Morissard, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Suspicion de fuites vers le RN : un mail jette des soupçons sur l'implication du préfet Moutouh</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261122-fuites-au-minist%C3%A8re-de-l-int%C3%A9rieur-un-mail-jette-des-soup%C3%A7ons-sur-l-implication-du-pr%C3%A9fet-moutouh</link><description>
La justice française soupçonne des fuites d'informations confidentielles du ministère de l'Intérieur vers le Rassemblement national. Un mail pourrait apporter des éléments sur le rôle de l'ancien secrétaire général de Beauvau et actuel préfet du Loiret et de la région Centre-Val de Loire, Hugues Moutouh, qui nie toute implication.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/83540fda-e696-11f1-ba48-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324374289119.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/83540fda-e696-11f1-ba48-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324374289119.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">fb9ec900-e680-11f1-8380-d59eaff5322f</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 14:28:27 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/83540fda-e696-11f1-ba48-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324374289119.jpg">© Ludovic Marin, Pool AFP via AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Présidentielle 2027 : François Ruffin jette l'éponge face à "l’impasse" de sa campagne</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261121-pr%C3%A9sidentielle-prenant-acte-de-l-impasse-de-sa-campagne-fran%C3%A7ois-ruffin-retire-sa-candidature</link><description>
À cinq mois de l’échéance, François Ruffin a annoncé, samedi, qu’il retirait sa candidature à l’élection présidentielle, prenant "acte de l’impasse" de sa campagne faute d’avoir réussi à imposer l’organisation d’une "grande primaire" de toute la gauche.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/049bdf84-e5d2-11f1-b9d8-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6J962D.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/049bdf84-e5d2-11f1-b9d8-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6J962D.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">34a0106a-e5d2-11f1-88ab-0f8d44227e2e</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 17:37:20 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/049bdf84-e5d2-11f1-b9d8-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6J962D.jpg">© Ludovic Marin, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Syndicats, jeunesse et gilets jaunes un peu moins mobilisés pour le sixième samedi de manifestation</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261121-en-direct-acte-vi-de-la-mobilisation-pour-la-jeunesse-et-contre-la-vie-ch%C3%A8re</link><description>
Pour la sixième semaine consécutive, syndicats, organisations de jeunesse et Gilets jaunes ont manifesté contre la vie chère, dans un contexte de colère sociale devenue européenne mais qui commence à s'essouffler en France. Le ministère de l'Intérieur a dénombré au total 82 500 manifestants dans l'Hexagone, dont 21 500 à Paris. La CGT parle de son côté de 150 000 manifestants dans le pays, 45 000 dans la capitale.
